function: Learned joint control of pinching-antenna positions and user transmit power to maximize the total data rate subject to a sensing SNR threshold and an energy budget (p. 1-3).
system: ISAC base station with N=3 pinching antennas on one waveguide (height 3 m), 6 single-antenna UEs, 1 sensing target, 28 GHz, TDMA, spherical-wave channel; no RIS (p. 2, 4).
method: Maximum entropy-based reinforcement learning (MERL): stochastic policy network, two critic networks, replay buffer, soft target updates; trained online over episodes of T=100 slots (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulated spherical-wave LoS channel of pinching antennas; UEs and target randomly placed in a 150 m x 150 m area; RL interacts with the simulator (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and testing (Table I: 6 UEs, 3 antennas, 1 target); Fig. 4 varies UEs from 6 to 12; retraining per case not stated (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: DDPG and TD3 (applied to the same problem). Non-learned: random positions and power (Random scheme) (p. 4).
metrics: Cumulative reward, normalized total data rate and normalized sensing SNR versus training episodes and versus number of UEs (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "Based on the spherical wave channel model", Eq. (1) taken from [4]; p. 4: "the communication UEs and sensing targets are randomly distributed". Own LoS simulator, no 3GPP or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 5: "under different numbers of UEs after the algorithm training is completed, with parameters fixed as specified in Table I" (Fig. 4). State and action sizes depend on M (Eqs. 10-11), so retraining per M is implied; no unseen-condition test or adaptation is stated.
q3_support: p. 4: "Random scheme: This scheme requires random values for the positions of the pinching antennas and the transmit power", plus DDPG and TD3; p. 5: "improved the normalized total data rate by 20.3% compared to TD3 algorithm and by 44.4% compared to DDPG algorithm".
q4_support: p. 4: "Fig. 2 shows the cumulative reward of the MERL algorithm with different learning rates (LR)." Only reward, rate and SNR curves are given; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime anywhere.
q5_support: p. 4: "the main parameters are summarized in Table I." Simulated environment only; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 5: the learned policy sets pinching-antenna positions and user transmit power to maximize the sum rate under a sensing-SNR constraint in an ISAC system (beams and resources serving both functions); area 3 is the alternative if antenna position is read as beam configuration, but ISAC is more specific. The BS has N=3 pinching antennas and the UEs have one antenna each, so the link is not single-antenna at both ends; no RIS (RIS is only named in the introduction as other flexible antennas, p. 1). q2 is borderline: Fig. 4 (p. 5) sweeps 6 to 12 UEs after training, but the paper does not say whether one trained agent was tested on other M, so 0; reviewer to confirm. Positions of UEs and targets are assumed perfectly known (footnote 1, p. 2). All 5 pages read, Table I and Figs. 2-4 viewed as images.
